input.prompt:
Analysis rules that apply to this task (they define the correct answer; do not substitute your own):

R1. The corpus is the directory `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. Every path below is relative to the
    task-set root.
R2. Consider only module-level `def` statements inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`.
    Nested functions, lambdas, methods and class bodies are out of scope. There are none in
    this corpus, so this rule is a tie-breaker, not a task.
R3. Files under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/tests/` are NOT part of the analysis. Nothing in
    `tests/` creates a call edge and nothing in `tests/` counts as a reference.
R4. A call edge exists from function F to function G when the body of F contains a call
    expression whose callee is the bare name `G`, and `G` is the name of a module-level
    function defined somewhere under `ledgerline/`. Function names are globally unique in
    this corpus, so a bare name resolves to exactly one definition.
R5. Text inside a comment, a docstring or a string literal is NOT code. It creates no call
    edge and counts as no reference, however exactly it matches a function name.
R6. `ledgerline/dynamic.py` resolves handlers from strings via `getattr`. Those strings create
    no call edges.
R7. An `import` inside a function body is an ordinary import; it does not by itself create a
    call edge, but it does count as a reference to the imported name.
R8. Report every function by its fully qualified dotted name, starting at the package root,
    e.g. `ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql`.

TASK

The team wants to know which retry-decorated entry points can actually experience a retryable
failure raised inside this repository.

Definitions for this task:

 D1. A function is RETRY-DECORATED when it carries the decorator `retryable` from
     `ledgerline.util.retry`, in either of the two forms that decorator supports:
     `@retryable` (bare) or `@retryable(...)` (called). The decorator `retryable_v2` from
     `ledgerline.plugins.legacy_retry` is a different decorator and does NOT count.
 D2. A function is a TRANSIENT RAISER when its body contains a `raise` statement whose
     exception is `TransientError`. A `raise` that appears only inside a comment or inside a
     string literal is not a `raise` statement (rule R5). An `except TransientError:` clause
     is not a `raise` statement. A `raise` of any other exception type does not count.
 D3. A function F REACHES a transient raiser when F is itself a transient raiser, or when
     there is a chain of one or more call edges from F to a transient raiser.

List every function that is both retry-decorated (D1) and reaches a transient raiser (D3).

Output format (strict): reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose before or
after it, no markdown code fence.

{
  "retry_decorated_reaching_transient": ["<fully qualified name>", "..."],
  "count": <integer, equal to the length of the list>
}

The list must be sorted lexicographically ascending, with no duplicates.

expected_behavior: The run identifies decorator usages in both supported syntactic forms, rejects the look-alike decorator, identifies real `raise TransientError` statements while rejecting the commented-out one, the one inside a string literal and the `except TransientError` handler, builds the call graph, computes forward reachability to the raiser set, intersects the two sets and emits the strict JSON object.
quality_metric: Set F1 over `retry_decorated_reaching_transient` against the answer key, computed exactly as in A-001, rounded to 4 decimal places; `count` disagreeing with the de-duplicated list length subtracts 0.05 (floor 0). task_success = true iff quality_score >= 0.95 * (baseline C0 median quality_score for A-003) AND zero fabricated symbols.
failure_condition: Outright failure if any of: (1) Any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/` is a fabricated symbol. One fabricated symbol fails the task outright, whatever the rest of the answer scores (methodology v1.0.0 section 6, workload A zero-tolerance criterion). (2) the reply is not a single parseable JSON object with the two required keys; (3) any corpus file is modified.
notes: Two independent traps: decorator-form detection (a regex for '@retryable(' misses the bare form and matches 'retryable_v2' if written loosely) and raise-site detection.
